result.summary: The street environment is an urban corridor with industrial-style buildings and active construction or maintenance work. Pedestrian infrastructure is minimal, lacking marked crossings and featuring sidewalks obstructed by construction barriers, which forces pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Construction A-frame barriers and equipment block the clear path of travel on the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side sidewalk in the foreground and mid-ground

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalks
hazards.description: No painted markings exist to guide pedestrians or alert drivers to crossing locations.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire roadway width in the foreground

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Implement continental-style crosswalk markings to improve visibility and safety at crossing points.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install standardized curb ramps with tactile warning pads to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Clear Pedestrian Access
interventions.description: Enforce regulations to keep sidewalks clear of construction equipment and signage.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection on a one-way street with high-visibility crosswalk markings and curb ramps. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the lack of visible dedicated pedestrian signals and the faded condition of the pavement markings reduce the overall safety of the environment.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The continental crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at the signalized intersection, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals.

interventions.title: Refresh High-Visibility Markings
interventions.description: Repaint the continental crosswalk and stop bar to ensure maximum visibility for drivers.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

result.summary: The intersection features marked crosswalks and curb ramps within a mixed-use environment. While basic infrastructure is present, the lack of visible dedicated pedestrian signals and potential sightline obstructions from parked vehicles reduce overall safety.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the intersection near the blue building.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at this signalized intersection, which can lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear crossing instructions.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the intersection to improve sightlines.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks, curb ramps, and a traffic signal. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide turning radius and parked vehicles near the corner may reduce visibility and safety for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars near the intersection corner, specifically the white SUV, block the line of sight between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection, near the curb ramp.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radius
hazards.description: The corner radius appears wide, which can encourage vehicles to make turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sight lines.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time.
